    • Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.
    • At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the manufacturer may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details.

    Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.

    At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the manufacturer may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.

    As 9to5Mac readers will likely remember, Apple widely advertised Apple Intelligence and AI-powered Siri features as part of its iPhone 16 launch campaign, going so far as to give its iconic Fifth Avenue store an Apple Intelligence-themed makeover and run an ad campaign starring Bella Ramsey.

    According to recent reports, this landed Apple in legal and regulatory trouble in multiple markets, including the US, where the company agreed to a $250 million class action settlement earlier this year, and Brazil, where it came under scrutiny from a consumer protection agency in May. Now, the company is facing potential penalties in South Korea as well.

    As a result of Seoul YMCA’s complaint, the KFTC conducted an investigation into Apple’s advertising practices. Today, the regulator confirmed (via MacRumors) that its investigators had submitted their findings and recommendations for formal deliberation by the Commission.

    According to the KFTC’s press release, investigators concluded that Apple advertised Apple Intelligence and its planned staggered rollout on the iPhone 16 website, but “concealed, downplayed, or omitted information material to consumers’ purchasing decisions.”.

    That included, per the press release (translation ours):.

    The press release also notes that Genmoji, Image Playground, “Siri with the ability to understand personal context,” and “Siri that provides step-by-step guidance” were not made available as advertised:.

    For example, Siri’s ability to understand personal context was advertised as being scheduled to launch first in US English by the end of 2024, as right now available in US English in October 2024, and as scheduled to support Korean in early April 2025.

    In reality, the feature was not debuted in US English until September 2026, with Korean language support following in October 2026.

    As a result, the investigators concluded that Apple’s conduct constituted a violation of the country’s Labeling and Advertising Act, which prohibits deceptive labeling and advertising.

    They recommended issuing corrective orders, including a prohibition on such conduct in the future, as well as imposing a financial penalty.

    They also estimate that Apple’s revenue associated with the alleged violation amounts to approximately 3.35 trillion South Korean won (roughly $2.5 billion), though the KFTC’s press release does not specify the amount of the fine.

    ⁠Yonhap noted today that the fine could reach roughly $48 million, while ⁠KBS reported that it could range between $21 million and $42 million.

    With the report now submitted, Apple has six weeks to submit its written defense before the Commission deliberates and makes a final determination on whether the organization violated the law and, if so, how much it should be fined.

    According to recent reports, in a statement to MacRumors, Apple said it had cooperated with the KFTC’s investigation, but disagreed with the conclusions. The company also highlighted the rollout of Korean-language support for Apple Intelligence last year and, more recently, for Siri AI.

Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Phoenix Suns guard Dillon Brooks and Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant exchanged words at the end of Houston's 116-104 win on Wednesday night.

    Durant was chippy all night, making sure to deliver extra trash talk against his former team.

    With less than 30 seconds left in the game, the Rockets led by 10. In a wild moment, Durant and Brooks weren't really playing; they were just talking to each other near halfcourt while the action continued.

    In a recent development, houston's Fred VanVleet hit a jumper with 23.8 seconds left to make it a 114-102 game in the Rockets' favor. Brooks and Durant were chirping at each other and got in each other's faces.

    The referees assessed each player a technical foul. Because Brooks had received a technical foul earlier in the quarter with 4:32 left, he was ejected. VanVleet drained a three and motioned to Brooks; they chirped and were both assessed technicals.

    Recent findings suggest that durant finished the game with 20 points and 10 rebounds. With 46.3 seconds left in the second quarter, the veteran forward drained a 3-pointer. That basket helped him become the fifth player in NBA history to score at least 33,000 points. He joins LeBron James (43,672 and counting), Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (38,387), Karl Malone (36,298) and Kobe Bryant (33,643).

    Industry observers note that the win moved Houston to 14-5. The Rockets return to action Saturday, hosting the Philadelphia 76ers.

    It has been revealed that the loss dropped Phoenix to 9-8. The Suns had won four straight before Wednesday's loss, and now turn their attention to taking on the Dallas Mavericks on Friday night.

    Breaking: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
    • During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
    • Also: Microsoft states its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

    During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

    Also: Microsoft states its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

    The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several upcoming Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

    “As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft mentioned. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

    Microsoft also confirmed Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

    In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s upcoming Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Microsoft stated the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

    Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

    It has been revealed that “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

    The manufacturer added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

    Nadella also confirmed a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Presently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

    “The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft stated of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

    Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

    Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

    While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can rapidly rack up costs when unsupervised.

    Microsoft revealed a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

    Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

    Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the tech giant’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft demonstrated how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

    In a recent development, “It starts with a fresh way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft stated. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

    Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

    “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft stated. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise aims.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several newly introduced models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company.
    • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
    • MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several newly introduced models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

    Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

    MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

    Recent findings suggest that “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, mentioned during the keynote.

    In a recent development, the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

    “No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman mentioned during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

    Recent findings suggest that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

    Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

    Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

    “Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the fresh coding model the company declared at Ignite.

    In a recent development, the company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

    Recent findings suggest that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

    Sources indicate that but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

    Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

    Recent findings suggest that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

    This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some key ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

    Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

    There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

    Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

    Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

    There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

    Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint.     Breaking: SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
    • In a recent development, grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
    • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

    In a recent development, grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

    In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

    Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

    Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

    “When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones stated. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this organization accountable.”.

    Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

    “It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

    Grok Imagine debuted on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

    Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

    Sources indicate that “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield remarked in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

    During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

    In a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX stated that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The firm said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

    Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

    Industry observers note that in July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The organization seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

    In a recent development, spaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

    It has been revealed that monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Substantial Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the tech giant intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

    Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving update. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

    The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch customers can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

    Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s fresh model worth it?

    Recent findings suggest that constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

    Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how quickly it can drain.

    Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

    The update improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

    In a recent development, that’s not the only Google Play Services enhancement that Wear OS smartwatch customers can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

    Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
    • According to recent reports, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
    • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

    According to recent reports, after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

    According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

    While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

    Recent findings suggest that starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

    It has been revealed that record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

    Uber says the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

    “Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

    Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

    “Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

    Uber claims it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

    In a recent development, uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Sources indicate that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    It has been revealed that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly vital sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 26, 2026

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mashable

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Moon is still looking almost full tonight, despite being a couple of days past the Full Moon.
    • 26, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 96% of its surface visible.
    • If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Kepler Crater, as well as the Tycho Crater.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Moon is still looking almost full tonight, despite being a couple of days past the Full Moon. It's now in its Waning Gibbous phase, meaning the illuminated portion we can see is gradually getting smaller each night.

    As of Thursday, Nov. 26, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 96% of its surface visible.

    If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Kepler Crater, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Endymion Crater, and the Posidonius Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 15 landing spots, plus the Descartes Highlands.

    Sources indicate that in North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

    Sources indicate that it takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a New Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

    New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

    Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

    First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

    Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

    Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

    Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

    Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

    Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

    According to recent reports, lois Mackenzie is a freelance reporter at Mashable. Over the years she has written for many publications, covering everything from the local news to the best pair of running shoes. You can find bylines in publications including Fit&Well, Metro, and Coach magazine, usually covering deals on everything from earbuds to TVs, or guides on how to beat your half marathon time.

    Lois also holds a Master's degree in Digital Journalism from Strathclyde University and obtained a Master of Arts in English Literature at the University of Aberdeen.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

    Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

    Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

    Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

    Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

    Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

    Industry observers note that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

    Recent findings suggest that shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

    Recent findings suggest that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

    The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

    Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

    Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

    Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

    Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

    Today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:05PM EST.
    • Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -0.91%) and Procter & Gamble (PG +0.44%) sell products that are bought in both good times and bad.
    • Warren Buffett was the former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%)(BRKB +0.37%).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Johnson & Johnson ›.

    Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -0.91%) and Procter & Gamble (PG +0.44%) sell products that are bought in both good times and bad. That's notable right now because the so-called Buffett indicator is more than two standard deviations above its historical average, suggesting a high risk of a downturn. If you are a conservative investor, safe-haven stocks in the healthcare and consumer staples sectors should be high on your wish list. Here's why.

    Warren Buffett was the former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%)(BRKB +0.37%). His long-term investment approach resulted in the organization achieving incredible long-term returns for investors. A key piece of the story was his penchant for waiting to buy until stock prices were attractive. That meant holding off during periods of overvaluation. The tool he used to determine the valuation of the broader market was the total value of the stock market divided by gross domestic product (GDP).

    According to recent reports, it is a rough gauge, at best. But when the Buffett indicator is at an extreme level, as it is today, it's worth taking a step back. You may want to reevaluate your portfolio, perhaps holding more cash. Or, if you want to remain invested, increasing your exposure to more conservative dividend stocks that have a history of holding up during periods of economic and market weakness. That's exactly what you'll find with J&J and P&G.

    One of the massive reasons to like J&J right now is that it is a Dividend King, with the longest dividend streak of any healthcare company at 64 years. It has successfully navigated multiple recessions and bear markets over that span. While the company has changed over the years, it currently focuses on the pharmaceutical and medical device segments of the broader healthcare sector.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In a recent development, the big story is that drugs and medical devices usually aren't optional purchases. Consumers are willing to pay for them because they improve their lives and can sometimes mean the difference between life and death. That makes J&J very resilient, a fact bolstered by its diversification across two business lines.

    Sources indicate that the one problem is valuation. J&J isn't cheap right now, but for conservative investors, it may be worth paying a premium if the lofty level of the Buffett indicator has you worried. That said, the healthcare giant's 1.9% dividend yield is well above the 1% you'd collect from the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.25%) and the healthcare average of roughly 1.3%.

    P&G is one of the world's largest consumer staples companies. It has a strong brand portfolio focused on paper products, toiletries, and makeup. Most of its products sit at the high end of their categories, which would seem like a risky place to be during an economic downturn. However, P&G has long focused on innovation, producing products that consumers are willing to pay more for. Notably, despite belt-tightening in many households today, P&G's organic sales grew 4% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

    And consumers aren't likely to stop buying their favorite toilet paper and toothpaste even if there is a downturn. At least that's what history has shown, helping P&G to increase its dividend for 70 consecutive years. Like J&J, that's the best streak in its peer group.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    P&G isn't exactly cheap, either. However, its price-to-sales and price-to-earnings ratios are roughly in line with their five-year averages. That suggests the stock is fairly valued right now. And the stock's 2.5% yield is above the consumer staples average of 2%, so you are getting a generous yield.

    The Buffett indicator is flashing bright red warning signs right now, given its elevated level. If that has you thinking about dialing back on risk, you should consider reliable dividend stocks from defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples. The best dividend records in those two sectors belong to Johnson & Johnson and Procter & Gamble. It's probably a good idea to start your search with these two safe-haven stocks.

    • If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.
    • Industry observers note that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

    Industry observers note that after reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.).

    For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

    The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

    The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

    Industry observers note that the Duo is a great gift for someone who’s remarked they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV demonstrates on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

    Sources indicate that the iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

    The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

    Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

    Sources indicate that perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

    Sources indicate that for the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.).

    The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

    Sources indicate that it’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

    Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

    It has been revealed that the Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

    Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

    Sources indicate that the phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

    In a recent development, for most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

    The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

    The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

    No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

    You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
    • Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.
    • OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

    Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

    OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Massive Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

    If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The tech giant already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

    Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

    According to recent reports, abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

    Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

    During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

    According to recent reports, at launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent consumers may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

    AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

    Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

    It has been revealed that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

    It has been revealed that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US people can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

    The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

    “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

    AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

    In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

    “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

    Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.
    • The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles.
    • According to recent reports, now, the partnership is ready to take its next major step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies noted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.

    The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

    According to recent reports, now, the partnership is ready to take its next major step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies noted. They strategy to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber prepares to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

    “Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an crucial milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”.

    Nuro states it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

    In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the manufacturer the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

    Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

    In a recent development, the Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

    Industry observers note that it’s been a major year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has debuted investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

    It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that apple is kicking off a upcoming and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

    Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

    Here are five helpful newly introduced features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

    First up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

    Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

    In a recent development, A fresh feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

    Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

    With a upcoming feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

    Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

    Sources indicate that the new app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

    Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

    Industry observers note that normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the new Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

    According to recent reports, some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone users. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

    By Manali Pradhan, CFA – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:17PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Industry observers note that anthropic (ANT +1.08%), the tech giant behind the Claude AI ecosystem, priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share. The number of customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue for Anthropic also increased from more than 950 to over 11,900 in the same time frame. The company had more than 1,900 customers that spent at least $1 million with it on an annualized basis at the end of the third quarter. This indicates that businesses are increasingly spending substantial amounts on the Claude AI ecosystem.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that however, Anthropic's revenue depends heavily on customer usage. Consumption-based fees accounted for approximately 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026. When businesses expand their use of Claude Code and other applications, they generate more revenue for Anthropic. However, customers could also reduce spending by limiting their token use or by switching to lower-priced AI models or competing services.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic reported net revenue retention of approximately 900% at the end of September. This highlights the rapid spending growth among the tech giant's existing customers. However, that calculation includes customers who generated as little as $1 in revenue in the prior-year quarter. Hence, the 900% figure may partly reflect rapid expansion from a low starting base rather than a growth rate Anthropic can sustain.

    Pricing is another concern. Anthropic disclosed that price reductions and contractual discounts that it introduced in the second and third quarters cut its revenue by approximately $600 million.

    With OpenAI's ChatGPT, Alphabet's (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%) Gemini, and other artificial intelligence (AI) competitors competing for enterprise customers, Anthropic will need to maintain strong usage growth without sacrificing too much on pricing.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, compared with a $974 million profit in the second quarter. However, adjusted operating income increased from $2.24 billion to $2.46 billion. The adjusted figure excludes stock-based compensation and certain other expenses paid in shares rather than cash. Such payments do reduce other shareholders' ownership stakes in the company.

    Computing expenses were a major concern. Anthropic's revenue increased sequentially by $5.4 billion in the third quarter, while computing and infrastructure expenses rose by $4.3 billion. Hence, the increase in computing costs was equivalent to nearly 80% of the additional revenue.

    Adjusted operating income, however, increased by only $228 million during the same period. Hence, investors need to consider just what fraction of Anthropic's future revenue growth will drop down to the bottom line as profits.

    In a recent development, anthropic's adjusted operating margin declined from 19% in the second quarter to 15% in the third quarter, mainly due to $5 billion in costs associated with leasing computing capacity under expensive short-term deals. The company expects to replace some of that with capacity from cheaper long-term arrangements. However, its continued payments for computing infrastructure could put pressure on cash flow.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic has firm commitments to spend approximately $900.9 billion on leasing computing and infrastructure, $451.6 billion of which is expected to be spent by the end of 2030. These commitments extend over several years, with some subject to conditions or termination rights.

    Anthropic generated $6.57 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026. However, it also spent $2.88 billion on equipment purchases and prepayments for leased assets and equipment. Hence, investors should watch whether Anthropic can generate enough cash from operations to fund its growing infrastructure needs.

    It has been revealed that anthropic had a market capitalization of approximately $1.1 trillion as of the close of trading on Nov. 24. Hence, the stock was trading at about 31 times its trailing-12-month revenue of $35.28 billion. The valuation multiple drops to around 13.4 times when using Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion at the end of October. However, the run rate reflects recent customer spending rather than revenues earned over a full year.

    Both metrics show investors are already paying a substantial premium for Anthropic's expected future growth.

    Industry observers note that another concern for investors who buy now is the looming increase in Anthropic’s float — the volume of its shares available for trading. Stakeholders who owned Anthropic shares prior to the IPO are subject to restrictions on selling their shares. But those lock-up periods will expire in a series of tranches from December 2026 through 2027. Each expiration date will allow those early investors to sell a larger fraction of the shares they own. This certainly does not mean these shareholders will sell quickly, but the additional availability of shares to be purchased could put downward pressure on the stock price. Future secondary share issuances could also reduce existing shareholders' ownership stakes in Anthropic.

    With all that in mind, I would suggest that you buy Anthropic only if you calculate that its valuation offers sufficient upside potential, despite moderating revenue growth and potential stock dilution.

    Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (475 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
    • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
    • In a recent development, the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the newly introduced Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

    Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

    In a recent development, the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

    There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

    The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the fresh Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

    According to recent reports, one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

    Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

    Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

    The Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

    Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

    UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

    Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

    Also: Google Wallet has a lot of upcoming tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

    It has been revealed that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.
