    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some upcoming money goals and make progress toward them.
    • That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.
    • In a recent development, “You’re probably not doing too much,” indicates Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some upcoming money goals and make progress toward them.

    That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.

    In a recent development, “You’re probably not doing too much,” indicates Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan. “It gets dark early. So those can be great months to lock into saving and not spend in excess.”.

    One important component of the Great Lock In is developing latest routines that will last well into 2027, states Jordan Mangaliman, founder and fiduciary wealth advisor at GoldLine Wealth Management in Fullerton, California.

    “We want a long-term habit versus a Band-Aid fix,” he indicates. “In today’s economy, money goes in and out so blindingly fast.”.

    In a recent development, ready to join the movement? Here’s how to get started.

    What’s your money moonshot? Maybe it’s paying off all your credit card debt or purchasing a home. Or spending less than you earn. Defining it is the first step toward achieving it.

    Recent findings suggest that “Spend a lot of time identifying what that goal is,” Baird says. “Everyone’s in a different position, so comparing yourself to what you see online might not be applicable.”.

    Even while setting ambitious money goals, it’s worth grounding them in reality, Mangaliman claims.

    If you want to save a larger portion of your income, he suggests trying the new saving pattern for a couple of months to see how it feels rather than saying you’ll do it forever and then getting frustrated.

    “It’s a marathon, not a sprint,” Mangaliman adds.

    Once you’ve outlined those big goals for your Great Lock In, create a budget to help you achieve them, Baird says.

    Sources indicate that he suggests combing through your previous credit or debit card spending to see where your money is going. Then you can decide what you want to change or shift. Using a tool like the 50/30/20 budget calculator can also help. This approach allots 50% of take-home pay toward needs, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and debt payments beyond the minimum.

    According to recent reports, baird suggests including saving as a line item in your budget so you don’t forget to do it. “Building that cost into your budget will put you in a better position later,” he states.

    Any Great Lock In should include growing your savings, because that makes achieving other goals easier, Baird states.

    It has been revealed that “Maybe there’s something you could cut in the short term to build up that savings,” he says. Good targets include subscription services, food delivery, entertainment and travel costs.

    Saving more is especially challenging in today’s environment, when everyday expenses like gas are higher than they were a year ago.

    Industry observers note that baird says that makes winter a good time to try to reduce costs. There can be fewer temptations to go out and spend money when the days are shorter and the temperatures are colder.

    Recent findings suggest that mangaliman recommends setting aside three to six months’ worth of expenses, although even a smaller amount is helpful. “Ultimately it’s about what you can afford,” he says. “It’s the foundation of your financial house.”.

    Along with building savings, paying down high-interest debt is another pillar of the Great Lock In.

    It has been revealed that with credit card interest rates higher than they were a few years ago, carrying credit card debt has gotten more expensive. “I would consider applying some savings to paying down debt, especially right now when your debt is costing you more than you can earn in savings,” Baird says. (You still want to reserve an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses.).

    “High-interest debt is one of the biggest thieves of wealth,” Mangaliman says. And one way to avoid turning to debt again in the future is to build up that emergency fund so it’s there for you if you need it.

    According to recent reports, even when you are committed to a Great Lock In, some hiccups along the way are inevitable. Success depends on continuing anyway.

    According to recent reports, “It’s like a diet,” Baird indicates. “Just because you ate ice cream on a Sunday doesn’t mean on Monday you can’t go right back to being disciplined again.”.

    “Be kind to yourself and do everything in moderation,” Mangaliman suggests. Just wanting to improve your finances is already a great first step, he states.

    In fact, he embraces the Great Lock In mentality himself. “There’s an old saying: It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” he says. “And you want to finish the year on a strong note so you carry those habits into 2027 and beyond.”.

    10 stocks we like better than O'Reilly Automotive ›.

    It has been revealed that investors might be jaded by artificial intelligence (AI), which seems to have been an even hotter topic this week with Anthropic's (ANT +1.08%) initial public offering. But it's never a bad idea to consider expanding your horizons and figuring out which other parts of the economy might deserve your capital.

    Industry observers note that O'Reilly Automotive (ORLY +1.32%) is a sleepy business, but it continues to operate at a high level. Revenue and diluted earnings per share were up 9% and 14%, respectively, year over year in the third quarter. The highlight was how well it's doing with professional customers, with sales to this group rising 12.7% last quarter.

    That last data point is a clear signal of O'Reilly's wide economic moat.

    It has been revealed that same-store sales (SSS), which strip out latest locations, rose 7.2% in Q3, after 5.6% growth a year ago. Management credited "share gains on both sides of our business.".

    Industry observers note that but the professional side is the standout. Sales to repair shops and other pros jumped 12.7% to $2.6 billion, roughly double the 6.2% growth in do-it-yourself (DIY) sales. Professional transactions grew at a mid-single-digit rate. More shops are placing orders, supporting volume, and not just paying higher prices.

    Time is money. A mechanic gets paid when a car leaves the lift. Every hour spent waiting on a part is lost revenue. So shops pick the supplier with comprehensive parts availability and fast delivery.

    That's where O'Reilly's moat reveals up. Its 6,758 stores are backed by 400 hub stores and 32 distribution centers. A regular store carries 24,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs). A hub can hold up to 115,000 SKUs and resupply nearby stores several times a day.

    Online sellers can't match that. The manufacturer has an intangible asset built over decades. Scale adds a cost advantage through vendor leverage and high-margin private-label brands.

    Operating margin widened to 21.4% from 20.7%, including the benefit from a one-time $39 million tariff refund. Management raised its full-year SSS outlook to 5.5% to 6.5% and plans 225 to 235 net new stores this year. Each one makes the network denser.

    In a recent development, the biggest long-term threat is electric vehicles (EVs). They have no oil to change and far fewer moving parts. Battery EVs were just 6% of new U.S. vehicle registrations in the third quarter, so the shift is slow. But it's real.

    Looking ahead, pro revenue growth is the number to watch. If it continues to outpace DIY, the moat is intact.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that O'Reilly has no problem growing profits. But the leadership team is also focused on shrinking the number of shares. The diluted share count fell by 5% over the past year, following $3.5 billion in buybacks through the first nine months of 2026. This ongoing trend is why EPS rises faster than net income.

    The industry backdrop helps, too. The average U.S. vehicle was 12.8 years old in 2025, according to S&P Global Mobility, a figure that has steadily increased. Older cars break down more often. That's a powerful catalyst for O'Reilly's 33 straight years (and counting) of SSS growth.

    According to recent reports, the stock, up 427% in the past decade (as of Nov. 20), is rarely cheap. It trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 28.6, versus a 23.3 multiple for the S&P 500. For investors with a five-year (or longer) horizon, I believe that premium is fair for a manufacturer this consistent.

    Industry observers note that it also offers quality exposure outside of popular AI stocks. Its fortunes depend on aging cars and busy repair shops, not data center spending. For investors looking to diversify beyond tech, that's a valuable trait. Boring businesses can make exceptional investments.

    4 Ways to Prep Your Finances Before the Next Tech Outage

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If your social media feed is anything like mine, you’ve probably seen a reel or two on nonperishable food and solar-powered generators after the recent string of tech outages.
    • Have I considered giving water-filtering straws as stocking stuffers this year?
    • In a recent development, but what about your money?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If your social media feed is anything like mine, you’ve probably seen a reel or two on nonperishable food and solar-powered generators after the recent string of tech outages.

    Have I considered giving water-filtering straws as stocking stuffers this year? Maybe.

    In a recent development, but what about your money? If your area was hit by a natural disaster or your bank had an outage, are your finances ready?

    Dan Stanush, senior financial planner at Charles Schwab in Asheville, North Carolina, recalls how fast financial conveniences disappeared after Hurricane Helene hit in 2024. “We lost power for three weeks and water for six weeks,” he said in an email. “And some local businesses could only accept cash or checks because card systems and ATMs were down.”.

    Industry observers note that don’t get caught unprepared. Here are the moves experts suggest to help you weather various types of emergencies:.

    Last week’s Chase outage was a good reminder that access to your bank balance can be disrupted. Stash at least enough cash at home — in small bills — to cover one week of expenses, notes Jeff Judge, a certified financial planner (CFP) with Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland.

    According to recent reports, if systems go down, ATMs can go down with them, said Eileen Olson, a CFP with Emerald Wealth in Daufuskie Island, South Carolina, in an email. Keeping cash in a safe at home is a good strategy, but it’s also smart to carry cash when you travel. (Remember when planes were grounded nationwide a week and a half ago?).

    In a recent development, “My parents and sister were traveling overseas on 9/11 and got stuck much longer than they expected,” Olson said. “After that, they always traveled with more cash.”.

    If your primary bank and its app were down, would you be able to pay bills? Having an account at more than one bank gives you an alternate funding source. Consider opening a high-yield savings account at a second bank or credit union for your emergency fund.

    Sources indicate that “This is the step I push hardest,” Judge states. “I had a client whose debit card, credit card and savings all ran through one bank, so when that bank’s system went down, she couldn’t even buy gas.”.

    Industry observers note that if you don’t want to open a second bank account, a second credit card from a different bank and preferably on a different network (i.e. Visa vs. Mastercard) can provide another way to pay for things. “If there’s a problem with one credit card network, I have a backup with two other credit cards,” notes Tony Steuer, author of “Get Ready! A Step-by-Step Planner for Maintaining Your Financial First Aid Kit.”.

    Make a printed list of your accounts, along with account numbers and key contact numbers. Include your bank, insurers, credit card companies and any financial professionals. Store the list with copies of essential paperwork, including insurance policies and their declarations pages, estate planning documents, legal certificates and identification — potentially in a fire-resistant file box.

    Keep a digital copy of your documents in a password-protected, encrypted spot as well. A password manager can store all of your login info.

    Joon Um, a CFP with Secure Tax & Accounting in Beverly Hills, California, suggests digital storage site Everplans to his clients, but there are a variety of sites that offer encrypted document storage.

    Sources indicate that take some time to write down how you’d pay for groceries, gas and medication if your usual payment methods weren’t available. What expenses would you need to cover first? What recurring bills are on autopay? Where would you keep the cash and any key documents you’d want to take with you if you had to leave home? Make sure other household members know where everything is.

    And set a reminder to update your records at regular intervals. Steuer, for instance, saves his account statements as PDFs and prints everything out once a year. “One of the big concerns is that people could conceivably break into your 401(k) and drain your 401(k) account,” he claims. Account statements could help if a hack affects any financial balances.

    It all adds up to a web of protection that (hopefully) you’ll never have to use.

    “The goal is not to anticipate every scenario,” said Schwab's Dan Stanush, “but to have enough flexibility to meet basic needs while systems come back online.”.

    Industry observers note that but I think Microsoft is being unfairly punished here. While many big tech companies are free cash flow negative due to heavy AI spending, Microsoft has affirmed it will remain in the black at least through fiscal 2027.

    That's a massive deal. And I think it's one reason why the tech sell-off in November presents an attractive buying opportunity for Microsoft before the end of 2026.

    Sources indicate that microsoft is one of the biggest players in the cloud computing space, holding 21% of the global cloud infrastructure market. That makes Azure the second-largest provider of cloud services behind Amazon (AMZN -3.12%).

    Sources indicate that in Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended Sept. 30, Azure revenue increased 48% from the previous year. Total Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion, up 30% from a year ago, and the firm's commercial backlog reached $677 billion.

    That's an enormous amount of business coming down the line, so Microsoft is spending freely to ensure it has enough computing capacity to meet demand. It spent $45.2 billion on capex in the quarter. But even with that spending, free cash flow remained positive at $18.6 billion. That's because Microsoft generated $58 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, up 29% from a year earlier.

    That's a substantial difference from some other tech companies whose AI spending has pushed free cash flow into negative territory.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Despite concerns about AI spending, Microsoft's underlying business is performing very well, thanks to its well-known software business. Nearly 4 million companies use Microsoft 365, including its popular office programs such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

    Industry observers note that those subscriptions provide recurring revenue, while Microsoft's Copilot AI products provide opportunities to sell more services to existing customers. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue increased 17% during the quarter.

    According to recent reports, that helped Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter revenue increase 19% to $92.3 billion, while operating income climbed 21% to $45.9 billion. Net income was $36.6 billion, up 32% from a year ago.

    It has been revealed that I don't expect Microsoft to slow its AI investments anytime soon -- and why should it? Microsoft Azure is generating substantial revenue, and Microsoft can continue to invest in the business while maintaining positive free cash flow.

    In a recent development, now down 13% from its all-time high, Microsoft offers investors an opportunity to buy a highly profitable company with two powerful businesses -- cloud computing and productivity software. I think the market is overlooking Microsoft's ability to finance its AI ambitions, and it's an appealing opportunity for investors before year-end.

    Tech Report: Should You Buy Tesla Stock Before December?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (802 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
    • Tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year.
    • Industry observers note that tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    Tesla (TSLA -1.18%) has had a challenging year. Despite its core electric vehicle (EV) business often performing better than expected, partly due to soaring oil prices, the company's shares have significantly lagged broader equities. However, the year isn't over, and there is a chance Tesla could finish 2026 with a bang, given ongoing developments. With that said, should investors consider buying the stock before December?

    Industry observers note that tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, now leads two publicly traded corporations, the other being Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), which went public in June. Rumors of a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX have been circulating since before SpaceX was public, but a comment Musk made during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call added fuel to the fire.

    According to recent reports, musk said that SpaceX and Tesla have formed independent special committees to discuss a potential merger between the two corporations. And more recently, five board directors from both companies have reportedly been discussing a potential all-stock merger that would make the combined entity worth about $3.5 trillion, with a deal possible by year-end. Importantly, this hasn't been confirmed by either organization. But it's still worth figuring out the potential benefits and risks of this proposed acquisition.

    Recent findings suggest that suppose SpaceX acquires Tesla at a 20% premium in an all-stock deal: SpaceX would have to matter a substantial number of new shares, thereby significantly diluting existing shareholders. Tesla's stock might rise, at least initially, while SpaceX's could decline unless investors believe the merger will generate enough synergies to justify the acquisition premium.

    According to recent reports, there are indeed some reasons to think that the combined entity could create more value than either would on its own. For instance, both Tesla and SpaceX are investing massive sums in artificial intelligence (AI). As a single entity, they could eliminate redundant investments and lower costs, while leveraging their larger size to negotiate better deals with suppliers.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In a recent development, also, some of Tesla's work, including its energy infrastructure and the Optimus humanoid robot, could be of immense value to SpaceX. So, that could be good news for the business' long-term prospects, although whether the proposed combined entity will, on balance, create more value is by no means guaranteed. However, one major source of uncertainty will likely come from regulators. The deal will probably attract significant attention from lawmakers, at least some of whom may try to stop it.

    Whether they succeed or not, it's hard to predict the impact on Tesla and SpaceX. And even as a combined entity, the company will be significantly exposed to regulatory risk across businesses such as space launch, satellite-based connectivity, EVs, and robotaxis.

    Putting aside the acquisition talks, Tesla's own business has somewhat attractive prospects. The tech giant's work in the robotaxi industry looks promising. Tesla released the Cybercab, a self-driving vehicle with no steering wheel, no pedals, and no mirrors, earlier this year. Provided it can scale its Cybercab fleet and capture a decent share of the market over the next five to 10 years, the robotaxi business could meaningfully contribute to the company's revenue and profits.

    And Tesla does have an advantage over other robotaxi leaders. The organization has a growing number of subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving software, which it offers to EV owners for $99 per month. A growing FSD ecosystem grants the company access to more data to train and improve its software. And as Tesla has pointed out, the FSD software is becoming one of the reasons people buy Teslas. That's great news for the company's future.

    Recent findings suggest that but one of Tesla's problems is valuation. At 157.3x forward earnings, the market has already priced in significant success from the firm's robotaxi ambition. So, I'd be skeptical about buying Tesla's shares at current levels. I'd prefer a much lower price. The potential merger with SpaceX changes very little, in my view, and actually adds significantly more uncertainty to the mix.

    The combined entity (if a merger does happen) will certainly be worth serious consideration, but investors with an average tolerance for risk and volatility shouldn't buy Tesla stock right now, whether or not they expect the manufacturer to merge with SpaceX.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively newly introduced corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    Industry observers note that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the organization like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo remarked. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The tech giant posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo stated.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Ferrari ›.

    Recent findings suggest that beating the S&P 500 sounds simple until you remember how good the index already is, since it has compounded at about 9.9% a year on a total return basis going back to 1928. So a stock that beats the index over 10 years needs more than a good quarter, it needs a business that can keep growing over the long term.

    According to recent reports, when I look for that kind of staying power in the consumer world, I aim for three things: a brand that people pay up for, a long expansion runway, and a management team that protects both. Here are three consumer stocks that I think long-term investors should consider for the decade ahead.

    Ferrari (RACE +2.96%) deliberately builds fewer cars than people want, and that scarcity is the heart of its economic moat, which is a durable advantage that keeps rivals from stealing its customers.

    CEO Benedetto Vigna mentioned in the third-quarter release that deliveries "reflect our clients' ever-deepening desire to make each Ferrari uniquely their own." Those personal touches add profit to every car without adding volume.

    Demand isn't the problem. Vigna said on the call, "We continue to experience a healthy demand across all geographies, with an order book that enters 2028.".

    The risks are a premium valuation, at roughly 36 times earnings, and the shift to electric models like the Luce, which has to win over buyers who love engines.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Hilton (HLT +0.52%) mostly doesn't own its hotels; it collects fees by managing and licensing its brands to owners through a franchise model, which is an arrangement where a business pays to use another company's brand and systems. That lets it grow without spending heavily on buildings.

    CEO Chris Nassetta mentioned in the third-quarter release, "We achieved our highest quarter ever for organic openings." He also said on the call, "Globally, Hilton is still less than 6% of supply providing a long runway for continued growth.".

    Travel is cyclical, though. CFO Kevin Jacobs mentioned, "RevPAR in China declined 5.4% in the quarter," referring to revenue per available room, which is a key hotel measure of how well rooms are filled and priced. Middle East conflict is weighing on that region, too, and the stock trades near 49 times earnings.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    It has been revealed that amer Sports (AS +2.56%) owns Arc'teryx jackets, Salomon shoes, and Wilson tennis gear, and every segment grew by double digits in its latest quarter. CEO James Zheng said, "I am very confident in the future outlook for our tech giant".

    The U.S. opportunity is what excites me most. Arc'teryx CEO Stuart Haselden noted that the brand has about as many stores in the U.S. as in Canada, which he noted "makes it very apparent the potential that we have to expand in the U.S." Management also said Europe's store traffic is a challenge, and higher freight costs are nibbling at margins.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, none of these companies will beat the market every year, but I think long-term investors should consider owning all three and giving their growth stories the full decade they deserve. Great brands tend to compound quietly.

    What ties these three together is pricing power, which is the ability to raise prices without losing customers, and I think that matters more over a decade than any single quarter's results.

    Ferrari's buyers wait years for their cars, Hilton's owners keep signing up for its brands, and Arc'teryx shoppers happily pay premium prices for gear that lasts.

    Industry observers note that there will be rough stretches, whether it's a travel slowdown, a weak luxury market, or a cold winter for outdoor sales, but investors who hold through those dips give each business time to prove its case. In the end, patience is the edge most investors give up too easily.

    Nvidia Is the Worst-Performing "Magnificent Seven" Stock This Year. Is It a Buy Before 2027?

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors have been on a rather unenjoyable roller coaster in recent weeks.
    • Founder and CEO for over 33 years, Jensen Huang, admitted on Nov.
    • Sources indicate that that same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Foelber – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) investors have been on a rather unenjoyable roller coaster in recent weeks. And every time the ride looks like it's nearing an end, there's another unexpected turn that unearths more questions than answers.

    Founder and CEO for over 33 years, Jensen Huang, admitted on Nov. 8 to being unfaithful to his wife, then resigned on Nov. 12, only to be brought back as CEO less than two weeks later on Nov. 23.

    Sources indicate that that same day, President Trump was on a phone interview with CNBC and took credit for speaking with Nvidia's board and helping convince them to bring Huang back. Trump said, "I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them. And I will tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago." Trump was referring to Nvidia's stock price and how it was easier to convince Nvidia to bring Huang back when the stock was cratering.

    Nvidia has rallied substantially since Huang came back as CEO, but Huang and Nvidia still face an uphill climb of federal, state, and internal investigations linked to Nvidia misleading investors and potential national security violations regarding advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips leaking into China through backdoor channels.

    The stock is still under $100 per share at the time of this writing and down 20% year to date -- making it the worst-performing "Magnificent Seven" stock in 2026. The Magnificent Seven consists of seven mega-cap tech-focused companies that include Nvidia, Apple (AAPL +0.43%), Microsoft (MSFT -1.25%), Alphabet (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), Meta Platforms (META +3.40%), and Tesla (TSLA -1.18%).

    Here's the simplest reason to buy Nvidia, and an argument for why it's best to keep the semiconductor stock on a watch list for now.

    Heading into this year, some investors were concerned that Nvidia would be unable to maintain its breakneck revenue growth rate and high gross margins. But hyperscalers continued to ramp up AI capital expenditures. And Nvidia has broadened its customer base to other enterprises, AI start-ups, AI labs, and neoclouds.

    Recent findings suggest that as a result, Nvidia's earnings growth began outpacing its stock price growth, compressing its valuation. But then the unthinkable happened.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's stock price has plummeted despite exceptional results and guidance for 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17, with revenue more than doubling from the third quarter of fiscal 2026. In the nine months ended Oct. 25, 2026, Nvidia generated $183.3 billion in net income compared to $77.11 billion for the nine months ended Oct. 26, 2025.

    Nvidia is on track to surpass Alphabet as the world's most profitable organization. It now trades at just 15.4 times forward earnings -- making it the cheapest Magnificent Seven stock despite having the highest gross margins and the fastest revenue growth rate.

    TSLA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    For context, the forward P/E of the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) is 17.3 -- meaning Nvidia is now priced like a value stock.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, buying high-quality companies on sale is an excellent way to compound wealth over time. Nvidia doesn't have to deliver blowout results to impress investors. In fact, its growth rate could fall substantially, and it would still be a steal at current levels.

    The issue isn't Nvidia's valuation -- it's investors' concerns about where the company could be headed over the next three to five years.

    Jensen Huang's sudden resignation exposed Nvidia's extreme vulnerability to key-person risk, governance failures, and an incapable board of directors. Going forward, Nvidia will need to change its structure to be less dependent on Huang, which could make it more rigid and less innovative but also protect long-term investors.

    Sources indicate that in addition to Nvidia-specific issues, there's also the risk that AI spending could decline considerably due to higher interest rates, which have made borrowing more expensive. With democrats taking control of the Senate and the House, there may be higher regulatory hurdles to accelerating data center construction. And there's the ongoing risk that compute demand will taper off as AI models become more efficient.

    Sources indicate that granted, Nvidia is incredibly well positioned to endure a slowdown because of its industry-leading position and rock solid balance sheet. But it could also lead to stagnating or declining earnings in the medium term, which would challenge Nvidia's valuation.

    All told, Nvidia simply has too many unknowns right now. Until investors get more clarity on the findings of the investigations, the tech giant's succession initiative for Huang, and the extent of its governance overhaul, Nvidia remains a hold.

    Heading into the new year, I'd rather buy high-quality Magnificent Seven stocks with a clear runway for future earnings growth like Alphabet, even if its valuation is more expensive than Nvidia's.

    According to recent reports, on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Legend Biotech (LEGN -0.23%) announced that net trade sales for CARVYKTI, its cell therapy for multiple myeloma, a blood cancer, grew 36% year over year to $710 million.     It has been revealed that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Investigational Latest Drug application, or IND, for LB2501, Legend Biotech's in vivo cell therapy that genetically modifies white blood cells directly inside a patient. It's seeing early clinical success, with a 100% overall and complete response rates at dose level 2.

    Recent findings suggest that international expansion is accelerating across 20 markets, and updated treatment guidelines favor cell therapy before antibody treatments. Management is keeping a close eye on doctor referral patterns and manufacturing capacity as overseas sales scale up.

    A deep cash cushion provides strategic flexibility as clinical trials evaluate earlier treatment settings and next-generation platforms. That balance sheet strength allows the business to scale production and fund research without taking on debt.

    #142520. Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor Stock Through 2030, This Would Be It.

    Not Nvidia. Not Micron. If I Could Buy and Hold Only 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor Stock Through 2030, This Would Be It.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.
    • For much of the last four years, semiconductor stocks have been some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.
    • In a recent development, although both companies have attractive long-term growth prospects, competition could complicate their investment narratives over the next several years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 26, 2026 at 5:54PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.

    For much of the last four years, semiconductor stocks have been some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. While Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) has become the king of AI accelerators, Micron Technology (MU -4.53%) is capitalizing on unprecedented demand for memory chips.

    In a recent development, although both companies have attractive long-term growth prospects, competition could complicate their investment narratives over the next several years. Moreover, as the AI infrastructure landscape evolves, identifying which chip architectures will dominate the market is becoming more challenging.

    Fortunately, there's one semiconductor tech giant that stands to benefit from virtually every major development across the AI chip landscape: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -1.96%).

    Between its graphics processing units (GPUs), networking equipment, and CUDA software ecosystem, Nvidia has an exceptionally durable competitive moat. Nevertheless, Advanced Micro Devices is investing aggressively in its Instinct accelerator portfolio, while some of Nvidia's largest customers are developing custom silicon.

    Broadcom has emerged as an crucial partner in the market for application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), most notably through its relationship with Alphabet and its tensor processing units (TPUs). Meanwhile, Microsoft and Amazon are also developing their own chip portfolios, including Maia, Trainium, and Inferentia.

    Another potential source of competition is Space Exploration Technologies' collaboration with Intel on Terafab. Terafab is Elon Musk's semiconductor manufacturing initiative that could eventually reduce SpaceX's dependence on third-party chip suppliers. Although commercial-scale production remains uncertain, the project underscores a growing appetite for vertically integrated semiconductor solutions.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Micron faces a different set of challenges. While the proliferation of generative AI has ushered in a memory supercycle, memory-intensive applications such as humanoid robotics and autonomous vehicles should introduce additional tailwinds over the next several years.

    Industry observers note that however, Micron competes against Samsung and SK Hynix in the high bandwidth memory (HBM) market. Furthermore, memory pricing has historically been cyclical, leaving producers vulnerable to fluctuations in supply, demand, and profitability.

    While Nvidia and Micron could both continue thriving, there is an alternative way to invest in the semiconductor industry without betting on a particular chip designer or memory manufacturer.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Unlike Nvidia and AMD, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) primarily manufactures semiconductors designed by other companies. Its customer base includes businesses spanning GPUs, custom AI accelerators, smartphone processors, and automotive chips.

    Recent findings suggest that against this backdrop, if Nvidia continues to dominate the AI accelerator market, TSMC benefits. Should AMD start to capture additional market share or custom ASICs become increasingly popular, TSMC still stands to benefit because it manufactures chips across these competing architectures as well.

    It has been revealed that interestingly, Taiwan Semi also has exposure to the memory supercycle. While the organization isn't a producer of conventional dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), its collaboration with SK Hynix involves manufacturing logic base dies for next-generation HBM4 solutions.

    It has been revealed that moreover, TSMC's advanced packaging technologies -- particularly its chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) platform -- play a critical role in integrating AI processors with HBM. As a result, growing demand for more sophisticated memory configurations creates additional markets for TSMC beyond traditional wafer fabrication.

    The most compelling aspect of TSMC's competitive positioning is the sheer magnitude of its market share. Industry estimates suggest that Taiwan Semi controls roughly 73% of the global pure-play foundry market. By contrast, the next closest competitor sits at just 6%.

    Although TSMC isn't technically a monopoly, its dominance gives it the characteristics of one. The company's manufacturing expertise, technological edge, production scale, and customer relationships are simply too difficult for the competition to replicate at scale.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    During the third quarter, Taiwan Semi generated $46.7 billion in revenue, representing 41% year-over-year growth. Meanwhile, the tech giant's gross margin reached nearly 65%, and its operating margin expanded to about 59%.

    TSM Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

    Management expects revenue to reach $53.3 billion in the fourth quarter, implying 58% year-over-year growth. These results illustrate how TSMC's manufacturing scale is translating insatiable semiconductor demand into robust profitability.

    Despite these impressive financial trends, Taiwan Semi stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 15.7. That valuation profile looks attractive for a business generating this level of growth and profitability while commanding such a dominant market position.

    Rather than attempting to identify which chip designer or memory producer will emerge victorious over the next several years, investing in the tech giant that manufactures many of the industry's most in-demand products looks like a compelling strategy.

    TSMC's architecture-agnostic business model, durable competitive advantages, and reasonable valuation make it a compelling semiconductor stock to buy now and hold through the end of the decade.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.
    • This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 12 of the NFL season kicked off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

    Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

    This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers.".

    Shortly after his appearance on the show, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that Rodgers was being released. The quarterback had mentioned on the show that he was "not going back to Pittsburgh." He was officially waived on Wednesday afternoon's transaction wire.

    We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have already ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for his third consecutive game with a groin injury, giving rookie Emmett Johnson the nod for a Thanksgiving contest with the Buffalo Bills.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

    According to recent reports, veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers passed through waivers Thursday and was not claimed. He is now officially a free agent after going unclaimed on waivers and is free to sign with any team.

    Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday and was subject to waivers. It is unclear which teams may be interested given how he conducted himself this week.

    News broke after 11 p.m. ET Tuesday night that Rodgers would not only be benched for the team's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos, but would also be inactive.

    Industry observers note that rodgers responded by joining "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon and going scorched-earth on head coach Mike McCarthy for about 35 minutes. The quarterback went off on McCarthy, accusing him of sleeping in meetings, not watching film, and saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" when breaking down a halftime huddle with players.

    In a recent development, while the writing was on the wall that Rodgers could be headed for a release, his interview with McAfee certainly sealed it. During his appearance, the quarterback even said he was not going to return to Pittsburgh.

    Recent findings suggest that the soon-to-be 43-year-old is now a free agent. Rodgers could land with a team that has quarterback injury problems or is right on the playoff bubble, but his conduct on Wednesday reportedly means that his options might be even more limited.

    Rodgers may have played the final game of his illustrious career, but his tenure with the Steelers will almost assuredly be remembered for his rant on Wednesday.

    49ers quarterback Brock Purdy did not practice on Thursday. It was his second straight day without practicing as he deals with an ankle injury. If he can't play on Sunday, it would be backup quarterback Mac Jones taking over against the Seahawks.

    Veteran wide receiver Mike Evans was upgraded to a limited practice participant after not practicing on Wednesday.

    The rookie quarterback continues to deal with a back injury and missed his second consecutive practice of the week.

    Recent findings suggest that if Beck misses Sunday's game, Josh Johnson is projected to be under center against the Commanders. Arizona did bring back Kedon Slovis this week after he was waived by the Ravens, but there hasn't been any indication that head coach Mike LaFleur is leaning toward starting Slovis after claiming him this week.

    Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert remains in the league's concussion protocol and missed practice on Thursday.

    If he doesn't practice on Friday, he will likely miss L.A.'s game on Sunday against the Patriots in which backup quarterback DJ Uiagalelei will likely be under center.

    The Jaguars' offense had some concerning entries on the injury report on Thursday.

    Wide receiver Parker Washington was limited due to a shoulder issue after not being on the injury report on Wednesday.

    Starting running back Bhayshul Tuten missed his second consecutive day of practice due to an ankle and foot injury.

    Jacksonville will have one more day of practice on Friday before statuses for Sunday's game against Tennessee are due.

    Sources indicate that the Steelers have had a tumultuous week, but got at least a spot of good news on Thanksgiving as veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. was activated off of IR.

    Pittman is expected to play for Pittsburgh against the Broncos on Friday afternoon.

    The veteran wideout was acquired from the Colts ahead of the regular season and promptly agreed to a 3-year, $59 million extension.

    Pittman has played in only three games this season and has been on IR since October 10 due to a left foot injury. He heads into this week's game with 89 yards on seven receptions and is still looking for his first touchdown as a Steeler.

    According to recent reports, it's a real shame the sports world learned about Mike McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant after Halloween. Given the absurdity of that revelation, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach's ice cream pal would have been a popular costume among sports fans looking to have fun with the moment.

    Recent findings suggest that thankfully, McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant is also perfectly in theme for the next big holiday. Thanksgiving is here in the United States, and, as you might have guessed, McCarthy's ice cream assistant is getting a little extra attention as fans and sports stars get ready to sit down for a day of gluttonous behavior.

    Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant was among the biggest names to reference McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant on Thanksgiving. Durant called the move a "great idea," and remarked he would be hiring an ice cream assistant of his own on the holiday.

    If you somehow missed the whole McCarthy saga, well, here's a refresher. After learning he was being benched by the Steelers, quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on Pat McAfee's show and completely blasted his own head coach.

    Rodgers remarked, frankly, a lot of wild things. He claimed McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings regularly and broke down the Steelers with a chant of "1-2-3 Packers" during their last game. Some of those claims have been confirmed by local media or McCarthy himself.

    In a recent development, but the ice cream sandwich assistant has even shadier origins. As all the Rodgers madness was popping off, former Steelers DT Breiden Fehoko claimed McCarthy had an ice cream sandwich assistant, someone responsible for bringing the coach an ice cream sandwich on demand. Fehoko claimed he received that information from a Steelers player.

    That report has not been confirmed by local reporters or McCarthy himself, though that's not going to stop sports fans from having a little fun.

    According to recent reports, 1. Fresh York Jets (Trade with Tennessee Titans) — Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State.

    In this deal, the Jets keep the No. 5 overall pick and package the Nos. 4 and 15 picks and a 2028 second-rounder to move up and tab Mestemaker as their QB of the future. Mestemaker has solid size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) with a good but not overwhelming arm. He plays in a friendly offense that he maximizes with his aggressiveness. He's a loose athlete with a knack for changing arm slots and the arc on his throws. He's had some inconsistent play over the last month or so as his aggression leads to too many dicey decisions. Yet he's the exact type of gunslinger who would be fun to pair with the Jets' assortment of talented young skill players.

    In a recent development, 2. Los Angeles Chargers — Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State.

    A season from hell can have its rewards!

    Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald noted what the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams might all be thinking: "I wish he would stay out one more week.".

    Donald was referring to Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons. A member of the Packers might also have applied the sentiment to Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett.

    Instead, the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game will feature a matchup of two teams who spent big to upgrade their pass rush recently — before injuries sunk their hopes within months.

    The Jaguars were without running back Bhayshul Tuten at Wednesday's practice as he deals with both a foot and ankle injury.

    With the chaotic week, Jacksonville benefits from a normal schedule, not having to play the Titans until Sunday.

    Tuten has played in all 10 games for Jacksonville this season. He has 642 yards and five touchdowns on 158 carries, and has added an additional 226 yards and three more scores on 21 receptions.

    San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday.

    Shanahan specified that Purdy does not have a high-ankle injury, but the quarterback may not be able to play Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.

    If Purdy can't start the NFC West divisional game, backup quarterback Mac Jones is expected to take over.

    San Francisco is 9-1 and leads both the division and the NFC. The 49ers had their bye week in Week 8 and have won three consecutive games.

    In a recent development, purdy is having one of the best seasons of his career. In just 10 games, he has already thrown more touchdowns (23) than in each of his last two seasons (20). Purdy has thrown for 2,624 yards and five interceptions, and has added 222 additional yards and two more scores on the ground.

    While the Rams continue taking injury hits on offense, they are getting a reinforcement on defense.

    Defensive end Kobie Turner has been activated ahead of Wednesday night's game against the Packers.

    Sources indicate that turner had been on IR because of a groin injury and last played on October 18. He heads into tonight's game with just seven sacks on the year.

    The Steelers have reportedly released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, per Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac.

    Rodgers' release was reportedly expedited after the quarterback went scorched-earth on former head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday.

    The schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway.

    There's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most important games, in terms of what's at stake.

    Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

    Industry observers note that aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

    Sources indicate that the Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the New York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

    This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the fresh deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

    Read more on Aiyuk's recent signing.

    The Chiefs are looking at another game without star running back Kenneth Walker III. Despite returning to practice Tuesday, Walker will reportedly not play against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, according to multiple reports.

    It will mark the third straight game Walker will miss due to the problem.

    In a recent development, prior to the injury, Walker was well on his way toward posting his finest season in the NFL. Through eight games, the running back already rushed for 872 yards and seven touchdowns. He also hauled in 26 catches for 172 yards and four receiving scores.

    There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

    It has been revealed that it's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he noted will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

    It was still abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

    It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

    In a recent development, the Steelers made the decision late Tuesday night to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. On Wednesday morning, the team began dealing with the fallout from that decision.

    It has been revealed that rodgers was reportedly not in the building early Wednesday when the Steelers held their morning team meeting at 8 a.m. ET, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor.

    Additional reporting suggested Rodgers was excused from going to team facilities the day after it was declared he was benched.

    It has been revealed that at that meeting, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy officially declared the quarterback change to the rest of the team. That decision was reportedly "not a popular" one within the locker room, per The Athletic.

    While Rodgers struggled this season, he was still well-liked by his teammates, per Pryor.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers revealed Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

    Aaron Rodgers will be inactive.

    The Eagles listed star running back Saquon Barkley as a full practice participant on Tuesday.

    The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

    The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 6:07PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Cgi ›.

    In a recent development, on its fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 11, 2026, CGI (GIB +1.40%) announced sequential revenue expansion driven by business acquisitions and managed services contract wins. For long-term investors, the tech giant's expanding backlog of $32.1 billion in contracted revenue provides steady multiyear cash flow visibility. Its operational strategy balances organic systems development with selective corporate acquisitions. Three key takeaways from management's comments highlight where the business is heading.

    In a recent development, long-term managed services, where clients outsource technology operations to CGI, provide predictable revenue streams that insulate the enterprise from short-term spending slowdowns. CGI reached an annual peak in managed services revenue as contracts signed earlier in the year transitioned from initial setup into full operational delivery.

    Recent findings suggest that public-sector demand is a primary growth engine for U.S. federal and state agencies. Government contracts accounted for a majority of upcoming orders during the quarter, supported by high customer interest in CGI's specialized public sector intellectual property (IP), which refers to proprietary software solutions built for specific agency workflows.

    It has been revealed that to complement systems integration and consulting (SI&C), in which consultants integrate third-party software and build custom IT infrastructure, CGI relies on niche acquisitions to expand its technical capabilities and regional presence. The firm completed five mergers during fiscal 2026 and plans to maintain an active buying cadence backed by low debt leverage.

    Client demand across core technology service lines continues to increase, supported by expanding global alliance partnerships. CGI relies on industry expertise and multiyear enterprise relationships to capture digital transformation projects while maintaining strict project pricing discipline.

    Strong operational cash flow and low debt leverage give CGI significant flexibility to pursue long-term shareholder returns. Management is balancing ongoing business acquisitions with share repurchasing programs and regular cash dividend payouts.
